text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementZoologySingle Orangutan Moms Set up Playdates for Their KidsAnd they go to considerable lengths to do itJCBy Jake Currie3:00 PM CDT on October 8, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleBeing a single mom is tough, but female orangutans don’t have any other choice. As far as parenting goes, male orangutans are pretty useless. They contribute nothing more than genetic material to their offspring before disappearing back into the forest. That leaves mom to teach their kids how to fish for termites, pick fruit, and access the other 250 odd food items that will allow them to survive on their own. This tutelage can take six to eight years, and it’s a lot of work—but that doesn’t mean there isn’t time for play. According to a new study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, orangutan moms go to great lengths to set up playdates for their youngsters.Read more: “How Social Learning Keeps Orangutans Fed”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
